title: Hobbs vs Airborne Time Divergence
dataSources: Pilot logbook (`flightlog:entry`), avionics telemetry (`avionics:telemetry`), flight-sim sessions (`flightsim:session`), pre-flight checklists (`preflight:check`).
app: Pilot and flight-sim telemetry — electronic logbooks (ForeFlight, LogTen Pro), Stratux / GDL90 avionics receivers, and Microsoft Flight Simulator / X-Plane SimConnect sessions — streamed to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=flightlog:entry
| eval ground_overhead=round(hobbs_hours-airborne_hours,2)
| stats avg(ground_overhead) as avg_ground_overhead, avg(airborne_hours) as avg_airborne by aircraft_type
| sort - avg_ground_overhead
description: Compares how much time is being spent on the ground relative to airborne time by aircraft type.
value: Ground overhead is not bad, but it is useful to know when it starts to dominate training efficiency or rental cost.
implementation: Log Hobbs and airborne time in `index=personal`; compare average ground-overhead gap by aircraft type.
visualization: Aircraft table of average ground overhead and airborne hours.
grandmaExplanation: It logs how much of your logged aircraft time is really ground time rather than time in the air.
